llm.summary: The bundled skill generates local blog outlines with limited file access; its optional unsigned Windows app requires separate consideration.

dimensions.detail: The script reads the supplied input and writes outline.md in the selected output directory. No network calls, credential access, or broad indexing appear.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled script requires only Python's standard library. The separate Windows app from the [publisher repository](https://github.com/rapidworker1/Multiple-AI-models-Toolkit) is explicitly optional and disclosed as unsigned; its binary was not inspected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions concern outlining and editorial checks, with no hidden execution or unrelated authority requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Only the generated output persists; no services, scheduled tasks, background workers, or privilege changes appear.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Local outline generation fits the purpose, but the template lacks the script's keywords field and the script fixes the target at 1,500 words.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use a dedicated output folder because an existing outline.md will be overwritten. Supply a keywords field and review the output because the template and script do not fully match. The optional unsigned Windows app is unnecessary for this workflow and is outside this review.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Downgraded: file writing is disclosed and limited to generating an outline in the user-selected directory. Missing permission declarations alone do not establish excessive authority.
[SQP-3] expected: Overridden: the description explicitly targets US writers, and the reference documents US-facing requirements, supporting the regional output instruction.
